newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Ambassador Hotel up on legal victory.
newsitem.headline: Ambassador Hotel up on legal victory.

text.p: Taiwan's Ambassador Hotel surged at mid-morning on Tuesday on news that it would gain some T$1.6 billion in compensation on its victory in a U.S. lawsuit, brokers said.

With 80 minutes left, Ambassador was up T$1.9 or 4.66 percent at T$42.7, while the overall index was up 0.24 percent. Turnover was 19 million shares, making Ambassador the second most heavily traded share.
Ambassador said a U.S. district court has ordered U.S. based Weichuan Construction and Development to pay it US$18.9 million plus 10 percent annual interest since October 1990.
Ambassador sued Weichuan alleging that it failed to meet contract terms in construction of a Los Angeles hotel for its U.S. subsidiary. Further details were not available.

The court ordered that Weichuan, owned by Taiwan investors but not affiliated with Weichuan Food, also should compensate Ambassador's U.S. subsidiary US$24 million plus interest over the same period, Ambassador said.
Taipei's China Times newspaper estimated the total compensation Ambassador could gain at around T$1.6 billion -- a boost for the company's bottom line.
"This surely would add non-operating profits to Ambassador," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.
"But the rise should be short-term, and we normally do not recommend buying the share as it is a relatively speculative share with asset play," Hung said.
